title: Checkpoints, fsync and the durability setting nobody should relax

videos.script: The write-ahead log makes a commit safe before the table has it. That leaves a debt. {{debt}} Every changed page is still waiting in memory, and the log keeps growing to cover them. A checkpoint pays the debt: it writes every dirty page to its file, and marks the place in the log where recovery would have to start. {{checkpoint}} This lesson watches one happen, then makes them happen too often, and reads the warning the server leaves in its log. {{warning}} Then it does what lesson 3 promised. It starts a stream of writes, kills the server with kill minus nine in the middle of them, and starts it again. {{kill}} You will read the recovery lines one by one, and check that every commit the client was told about is still there. {{recovery}} Last, two settings that trade safety for speed. One loses a fraction of a second of work in a crash. The other can lose the whole database. You will measure the first, and learn why nobody should touch the second. {{fsync}}
